facility_roles.quote: The High Altitude GAmma-Ray (HAGAR) array is a wavefront sampling array of 7 telescopes, set-up at Hanle, at 4270 m amsl, in the Ladakh region of the Himalayas (Northern India).

intervals.label: regular observations (documented to December 2017)
intervals.note: Start: regular source observations since September 2008. End: the Crab dataset of the 2019 HAGAR paper runs from October 2008 to December 2017 (arXiv:1902.01081); that is the end of the documented data, not of observations.
intervals.quote: Regular source observations are running since September 2008.

intervals.label: operation after 2017 (not documented)
intervals.note: No source fetched dates the end of HAGAR observations. A 2024 review describes the array in the present tense; the status is carried forward from that and not confirmed.
intervals.quote: The HAGAR telescopes (Singh, et al. 2019) are located in Hanle in the Himalayas at 4500 m above sea level, on the same site as the 21 m diameter Cherenkov imaging telescope MACE

quantity.quote: consists of an array of seven atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes located at the center and corners of a hexagon inscribed in a circle of 50 meter radius
The total reflector area of all seven telescopes is about 31 m2
set-up at Hanle, at 4270 m amsl
was designed to reach a relatively low threshold (currently around 200 GeV) with quite a low mirror area (31 m2)

name: HAGAR
notes: No collaboration is recorded: the sources name none. HAGAR was built by TIFR, IIA, BARC and SINP (author affiliations, Astrophys. Space Sci. Trans. 7, 501).
No official HAGAR website is recorded: none was found that could be fetched.
Unresolved: whether HAGAR is still observing in 2026; see the second interval.

physics_goals.quote: was designed to reach a relatively low threshold (currently around 200 GeV) with quite a low mirror area (31 m2)
physics_goals.value: Detect very high energy gamma rays from the Crab Nebula and blazars with a wavefront-sampling array at high altitude, to reach a low threshold with a small mirror area.

summary.plain: An array of seven small telescopes at Hanle in Ladakh, 4270 metres up in the Himalayas, that records the wavefront of the faint light flashes from gamma-ray air showers. It has been observing since 2008.
summary.technical: HAGAR (High Altitude GAmma Ray) wavefront-sampling array of seven non-imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (31 m2 total mirror area, threshold about 200 GeV) at Hanle, 4270 m; first phase of the HIGRO project; regular observations since September 2008; Crab detected at about 20 sigma (arXiv:1902.01081).

unique_capabilities.quote: was designed to reach a relatively low threshold (currently around 200 GeV) with quite a low mirror area (31 m2)
unique_capabilities.value: The first array of atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes established at such a high altitude, reaching a relatively low threshold with a small mirror area.
